description: An indicator of whether the radial artery was used as the arterial access site during a Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI) procedure, in accordance with the National Cardiac Registry (NCR) guidelines.
rationale: The NCR tracks arterial access sites to benchmark clinical practice, as radial access is increasingly recognised as best practice for PCI due to its association with reduced bleeding complications compared to femoral access. This flag should be recorded for all admitted patient care episodes where a PCI is performed. If multiple access sites are attempted, code as 1 (Yes) if the radial artery was successfully used to complete the procedure.

description: Percentage of PCI episodes presenting with ST‑Elevation Myocardial Infarction (STEMI)
rationale:
The proportion of PCI episodes presenting with STEMI provides essential case‑mix context for interpreting PCI activity, outcomes, and timeliness indicators. STEMI cases represent higher acuity, time‑critical presentations and should be reported separately to avoid inappropriate comparison with non‑STEMI or elective PCI cohorts.
This indicator supports transparent interpretation of downstream quality indicators (e.g. door‑to‑device time, mortality) and aligns with NCR cohort definitions.
numerator: Number of PCI procedures where Type of Acute Coronary Syndrome (ACS) is recorded as STEMI.
denominator:
Total number of eligible PCI episodes reported to the registry within the reporting period.

description: The time from the patient's presentation to the PCI room and completed reperfusion via coronary intervention.
rationale: Reperfusion treatment for patients with STEMI is time critical and excessive delays can have serious adverse impacts on patient outcomes.
poster_label: Median Door to Device time was {s} min

description: In-hospital major bleeding during or immediately after an admission for PCI
rationale: May indicate unintentional misadventure has occurred during the procedure, exacerbation or other cause of major bleed.
numerator: Number of patients in the denominator who had a major bleed during or after the PCI
denominator: All patients undergoing PCI during the selected observation period

description: The 30-day all-cause mortality for adult patients undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI)
rationale: May indicate higher risk vs benefits of PCI procedures for some higher risk patients
numerator: The number of patients in the denominator who died during the 30 days after the procedure including: 1: All deaths occurring during hospitalisation in which the procedure was performed and up to 30 days, 2: deaths occurring after discharge from hospital within 30 days of the procedure
denominator: All patients undergoing PCI during the selected observation period

description: Proportion of patients with documented referral prior to discharge to a cardiac rehabilitation or alternative secondary prevention program
rationale: Cardiac rehabilitation or other secondary prevention programs are recommended to reduce risk of subsequent cardiac events. All patients with cardiovascular disease should have access to and be actively referred to comprehensive ongoing prevention and cardiac rehabilitation services.
numerator: Total number of patients with a diagnosis of ACS with a documented referral prior to discharge to a cardiac rehabilitation or an alternative secondary prevention program.
denominator: Total number of patients with a final diagnosis of ACS who are discharged from hospital
poster_label: Evidence of referral to Cardiac Rehab was available in {s} patients

description: Proportion of discharged patients on dual antiplatelet therapy (DAPT) with no clear documented contraindication for aspirin or P2Y12 inhibitor.
rationale: ACS patients on aspirin and dual antiplatelet therapies have a reduced risk of secondary cardiac events. ACS patients on aspirin and dual antiplatelet therapies have a reduced risk of secondary cardiac events. The Guidelines for the management of acute coronary syndromes 2006 (Acute Coronary Syndrome Guidelines Working Group 2006) recommend that, before separation, patients with an ACS should be initiated on a medication regimen, including antiplatelet agent(s), beta-blocker, angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitor, statin and other therapies as appropriate.
numerator: Total number of patients with a diagnosis of ACS who are prescribed aspirin or other dual antiplatelet therapy on hospital discharge
denominator: Total number of patients with a final diagnosis of ACS who are discharged from hospital

description_short: Time from diagnostic ECG to PCI mediated reperfusion.
description: For STEMI patients, the time from diagnostic ECG to first balloon inflation or (where guidewire or device prevented from crossing by lesion) the time the guide catheter was introduced.
rationale: The aim of reperfusion is the timely restoration of coronary flow. Primary PCI is preferred for reperfusion therapy in patients with STEMI if it can be performed within 90 minutes of first medical contact (diagnosis)2.

description: The rate of stroke for patients undergoing Percutaneous Coronary Intervention (PCI) within the same episode of care.
rationale: To indicate whether a new stroke has occurred during or after the PCI prior to discharge.
numerator: Number of patients in the denominator who had a stroke during or after the PCI
denominator: All patients undergoing PCI during the selected observation period

description: In-hospital deaths for patient admitted for PCI.
rationale: A measure of risk of PCI procedures
numerator: Number of PCI patients who deceased in hospital during the same PCI admission during the refence period.
denominator: Total number of PCI inpatients in the reference period.

description_short: had an unplanned cardiac readmission within 30 days after PCI
description: The rate of unplanned cardiac readmissions within 30 days of percutaneous coronary intervention being performed.
rationale: 30-day readmission could be suggestive of procedure related adverse outcomes and needs to be differentiated from planned readmissions for PCI or CABG.
numerator: Number of patients in the denominator who experience an urgent readmission to any hospital on or before the 30th day following the date of discharge from the index PCI procedure.
denominator: All patients undergoing PCI who were discharged alive after the index PCI.

description: The rate of unplanned readmission for revascularisation within 30 days of PCI admission
rationale: May indicate previous revascularisation was unsuccessful and required repeat procedure.
numerator: Number of patients who were readmitted within 30 days of last PCI admission
denominator: All patients who underwent PCI within the reference period.

description_short: Patients without contraindication discharged on lipid-lowering therapy
description: Proportion of patients with a final diagnosis of ACS who are prescribed lipid lowering therapy at hospital discharge.
rationale: Lowering lipid levels is an effective primary and secondary prevention treatment for vascular events, including stroke1.
numerator: Total number of patients with a diagnosis of ACS who are prescribed a statin or other lipid lowering therapy at hospital discharge.
denominator: Total number of patients with a final diagnosis of ACS who are discharged from hospital
